blocks.text: David's refusal to kill Saul is part of a repeated pattern: twice he has the opportunity to do so, yet he restrains himself because Saul remains the LORD's anointed. In this chapter, that conviction explains why David takes Saul's spear and water jar as proof of access to the camp but will not harm him.

This episode stands within the larger movement of 1 Samuel: from Eli's failing priestly house, through Samuel's prophetic leadership and Saul's rejected kingship, to David's anointing, rise, exile, and Saul's death.
